scope.text: Interior design of a three-bedroom apartment: joinery, finishes, lighting, sanitaryware and loose furniture.
Renovation of two bathrooms, including waterproofing and plumbing alterations.
Civil changes limited to non-structural partitions unless a structural engineer and the housing society approve otherwise.

targetCompletion.note: Client's hoped-for move-in date. Not yet programmed against approvals and lead times.

range.source: Intake meeting, 12 Aug 2026 — stated by Rohan Mehta

includesGst.note: Not discussed. Confirm whether the range includes GST.

budget.covers: Interior works, joinery, finishes, lighting and sanitaryware. Excludes appliances and loose decor.

designBrief.summary: A calm, warm and durable home for a three-generation family: natural materials, honest craft and generous daylight, with the parents' suite designed for safe, independent use as Rohan's mother grows older.

objectives.text: Create a calm, uncluttered backdrop for a busy family, with generous concealed storage.
Make the parents' bedroom and bathroom safe and comfortable for an older user without looking clinical.
Seat 10 to 12 guests for weekend lunches without permanently oversized furniture.
Favour durable, repairable materials that age well in Bengaluru's climate, including the monsoon.

styleDirection.narrative: Honed stone underfoot, warm timber, lime-finished walls and restrained metalwork. Light is layered and warm; colour comes from materials rather than paint.

references.text: Clients responded well to images of South Indian courtyard homes with red oxide floors and teak joinery.

notes.text: Material choices are conceptual. No physical samples have been approved yet.

functionalRequirements.text: East-facing pooja unit within the living room.
functionalRequirements.source: Brief approval, email from Rohan Mehta, 7 Sep 2026

functionalRequirements.text: Study corner for video calls with controllable daylight and warm, even light on the face.
Closed footwear storage at the entrance for about 20 pairs.

constraints.text: Housing society rules restrict working hours and debris removal.
No structural changes without a structural engineer's approval and the housing society's no-objection certificate.

range.source: Intake meeting, 12 Aug 2026 — stated by Rohan Mehta

includesGst.note: Not discussed. Confirm whether the range includes GST.

budget.covers: Interior works, joinery, finishes, lighting and sanitaryware. Excludes appliances and loose decor.

timeline.text: Clients hope to move in by 31 March 2027.
Lead times for sanitaryware are unknown until models are confirmed.

recommendations.text: Use honed Kota stone as the continuous floor in the living, dining and bedroom areas.
recommendations.rationale: Locally sourced, durable and cool underfoot, and matches the clients' preference for a soft natural floor.

recommendations.text: Design the parents' bathroom for level access with a linear drain and a fixed glass screen.
recommendations.rationale: Removes the step into the shower and reduces trip risk for an older user.

assumptions.text: Slab soffit heights are similar across the apartment (about 2,850 mm), based on the bathroom survey.
assumptions.source: Site survey of the parents' bathroom, 22 Aug 2026

openQuestions.text: Is there enough depth below the bathroom floors for level-access showers?

issues.title: Wall-hung WC needs a wall outlet; the existing WC has a floor outlet
issues.description: Converting the outlet depends on the sunken depth and the route to the soil stack, neither of which is confirmed.

issues.title: Bathroom door clear opening is 700 mm
issues.description: Below the 750 mm minimum in the planning guidance and well below the 900 mm recommended for a walking aid. Widening needs a check of the lintel.
